title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 177 (Defaulting pawnor’s right to redeem)

content.overview: Section 177 provides that if a time is stipulated for the payment of the debt, or performance of the promise, for which the pledge is made, and the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt or performance of the promise at the stipulated time, he may redeem the goods pledged at any subsequent time before the actual sale of them; but he must, in that case, pay, in addition, any expenses which have arisen from his default.
content.glance: Defaulting pawnor may redeem the goods at any time before actual sale by paying the amount due plus expenses arising from the default.
content.study: If a time is stipulated for the payment of the debt, or performance of the promise, for which the pledge is made, and the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt or performance of the promise at the stipulated time, he may redeem the goods pledged at any subsequent time before the actual sale of them; but he must, in that case, pay, in addition, any expenses which have arisen from his default. Current-law framing: right of redemption survives default until actual sale, subject to payment of default expenses.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If a time is stipulated for the payment of the debt, or performance of the promise, for which the pledge is made, and the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt or performance of the promise at the stipulated time, he may redeem the goods pledged at any subsequent time before the actual sale of them; but he must, in that case, pay, in addition, any expenses which have arisen from his default.

examples.title: Redemption before sale
examples.body: Pawnor defaults but redeems before actual sale by paying the amount due plus expenses from the default under Section 177.

hypotheticals.question: Pawnor defaults but the goods have not yet been sold. May he still redeem?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 177 allows redemption at any time before the actual sale, upon payment of the amount due and any expenses arising from the default.
